svg.aria-label: Rung 100, sizing measured but not deployed: an Application Load Balancer is the front door in front of two to four stateless API tasks on ECS Fargate; the API writes to a job queue whose depth is the backlog signal, agent worker tasks holding about fifty slots drain it and make the bounded language-model calls, session and rate-limit state moves out to Redis, and Aurora runs with a minimum capacity above zero plus one reader.

g.title: users — about 100 concurrent askers, roughly 5–10k monthly users at a 1–2% concurrency rule of thumb
Application Load Balancer plus WAF — the front door, doing the job an API Gateway would otherwise do. Its idle timeout goes to 4,000s, which is what lets a 90-second answer or an SSE stream survive.
API tier — the same FastAPI app as an ECS service on Fargate: 2–4 stateless tasks autoscaled on CPU and request count
job queue — Redis Streams or SQS, with an admission depth that sheds past the cap; queue depth is the backlog signal autoscaling reads
agent workers — about 50 slots, for example 8–12 tasks × 4–6 concurrency; drain time follows the measured formula, ceiling of N over slots, times service time
Aurora — minimum capacity above zero kills the cold start, one reader carries Explore and SQL; pgvector stays in the database
Redis — sessions, rate limits and the demo pack out of process memory; this is the seam ConvFinQA's limits module already names
LLM provider — in-flight calls are bounded by the worker slot count, which is where a single provider's rate limit starts to matter
